decisions: Single shared catalog.catalog_terms table discriminated by catalog_type (see prior note) — verified end-to-end against a real Postgres instance: migration up/down, idempotent reseed, and category parent/child hierarchy all confirmed via direct DB queries.

card-catalog/product-catalog facet counts: for catalog-term-backed facets (occasion/style/format/colorFamily/accessTier for cards; category/occasion/recipient/personalization/material/rush for products) each facet excludes only its OWN active filter when computing its own option counts (others AND'd in) — verified by e2e test; category facet counts are descendant-inclusive via a recursive closure CTE.
price/preparation/rating are filter-only (no enumerated facet-count group) since they are continuous ranges, not discrete catalog options — documented in ListProductsFilter/product.repository.ts.

Each product modeled with exactly one representative variant in seed data (schema supports many); effective price/prep/rush read from the cheapest available variant via a LATERAL join in list(), and from an EXISTS-with-combined-conditions clause in filtering, per code comments in typeorm-product.repository.ts.

Fixed a real bug found via e2e testing: card-catalog's buildMatchConditions hardcoded a param-index offset assuming a caller-reserved $1, breaking computeAccessTierFacet (which has no such reservation) with 'could not determine data type of parameter $1' whenever a search-only or filter-only facet query ran — fixed by parameterizing startIndex per call site (0 vs 1), matching the pattern already used correctly in product-catalog.

Fixed a real bug: ListProductsUseCase collapsed a requested-but-nonexistent categoryIds filter to an empty array after descendant resolution, which the repository treats as 'no filter' — now falls back to the original nonexistent ids (still non-empty) so the filter still correctly matches zero products instead of silently ignoring the filter.
